subject.title: Owner-signed responsibility gates for assistant memory, actions, skills, and evidence reuse

question: Should OpenClaw own a core responsibility-state contract for durable memory/evidence reuse, or keep this as plugin/ClawHub experimentation until a narrower missing core API is proposed?
rationale: This cannot be safely resolved as a small repair because it crosses durable memory schema, retrieval semantics, plugin SDK/API contracts, action approvals, UI auditability, public config, and security policy.

options.title: Sponsor Core RFC
options.body: Keep this issue open as the umbrella for a security/product design that defines owner-confirmed states, revocation, and extension points before implementation.

options.title: Require Narrow API Gap
options.body: Ask contributors to prototype SCBKR/UMP-style flows as plugins and return only with specific missing plugin or memory API seams.

options.title: Reject Broad Layer
options.body: Close the umbrella direction and keep only narrower existing provenance, taint, and approval issues for concrete defects.

recommendation.title: Sponsor Core RFC
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open as the umbrella for a security/product design that defines owner-confirmed states, revocation, and extension points before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest current-main routing evidence is recent ownership of the memory, plugin hook, security-doc, and VISION surfaces this decision would affect.
